text:
Maxim Shabanov took the long way to a regular NHL job: undrafted, a 67-point season for Traktor Chelyabinsk in the KHL, then 44 games with the Islanders last season. In Minnesota he has become a power-play weapon. He is on the ice for 71% of the Wild's power-play chances, up from 27% last season, and 9 of his 13 points have come with the man advantage.

He is hot, and much of it is earned. He has 7 points (6 goals) in his last ten games, where we'd expect about 5.7 at his ice time, and his own chances are up too. Hockey Wilderness has argued the Wild are "Leaving Production On the Table" with him.

The warning is the finish. He has 8 goals on 4.55 expected goals, our measure of the quality of his chances, and he is shooting 25% after 9% last season. Our numbers flag that as due to cool. At 5-on-5, Minnesota has taken 46.9% of expected goals with him on the ice, 7.4 points worse than without him. The power-play role is the real part.
headline: Shabanov has found a home on Minnesota's power play
